heard: A cosmic death star was once feared to be pointed at Earth. Deep in the constellation Sagittarius lies WR-104, located about 8,400 light years from Earth. At its heart, a massive wolf-rayet star and an ob-companion orbit each other every eight months. Their powerful stellar winds slammed together, creating a spinning pinwheel nebula over 200 astronomical units wide. Early imaging suggested Earth was looking directly down the rotational axis, sparking panic over a lethal gamma-ray burst. Recent Keck Observatory research revealed that the actual stellar orbit is tilted 30 to 40 degrees away from us. Earth is safely out of the firing line, proving why a cosmic death star was once feared to be pointed at Earth.
